bib.title: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images

read.skipped: references after [32] skimmed only; no supplementary included in PDF

question: How well can existing scene-text VQA and reading-comprehension models answer questions about real document images, and how far are they from humans?
hypothesis: Answering document questions needs reading text and interpreting it within layout and structure, which existing models handle poorly.
contributions: DocVQA, 12,767 document images with 50,000 questions and answers, categorised by reasoning requirement
Baselines: heuristics, upper bounds, human performance, scene-text VQA models and NLP models

method.summary: Pages from UCSF Industry Documents Library were hand-picked and annotated by remote workers in three stages with extractive answers. Baselines are heuristics, LoRRA and M4C trained via MMF, and BERT QA models fine-tuned on SQuAD-style serialized OCR text.

datasets.name: DocVQA
datasets.split: 80-10-10 random: train 39,463 q / 10,194 images; val 5,349 q / 1,286 images; test 5,188 q / 1,287 images
datasets.source: UCSF Industry Documents Library; licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: OCR from a commercial OCR application, serialized top-left to bottom-right, space-separated; answer span approximated by first match of answer string (TriviaQA approach)

models.name: LoRRA
models.architecture: bottom-up/top-down attention with OCR-token attention and copy from OCR
models.init_from: GloVe, ResNet-152 (ImageNet), Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome), FastText
models.vocab: 4,341 answers (occur more than once in train)

models.name: M4C
models.architecture: multimodal transformer with iterative answer decoding and OCR pointer
models.init_from: BERT question embedding, Faster R-CNN, FastText, PHOC
models.vocab: 5,000 most frequent answer words in train

training.objective: extractive span prediction (BERT); LoRRA/M4C as original works
training.hardware: 2x Nvidia GeForce 1080 Ti (bert-base); 4 GPUs (bert-large, unspecified type)

other.LoRRA_M4C: official MMF implementations, training settings and hyperparameters same as original works

metrics.name: ANLS
metrics.definition: Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity, from ST-VQA; soft match so OCR errors are not severely penalized; primary metric

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: percentage of questions where prediction exactly matches any target answer

eval.protocol: single run per config on val and test; human answers on all test questions from a few volunteers; no seeds or significance tests reported

evidence.quote: We use Adam optimizer [24] with a learning rate of 5e −05.

limits: Answers are extractive spans copied verbatim from the page, so abstractive and numeric-reasoning questions are not covered.
All baselines depend on one commercial OCR; OCR substring UB of 87% caps text-only models.
Baselines are scene-text VQA and text-only BERT models; no layout-aware pretrained document models.
Human performance from a few volunteers at the authors' institution.
Per-question-type scores are shown only as a bar chart (Fig 8), no numbers.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; GPU type for bert-large not stated; licence not stated.
Authors note models fall short specifically on questions needing document structure, figures, photographs and handwriting.
